author: Barons of King John, with Archbishop Stephen Langton

_quarry.description: Charter of liberties sealed by King John at Runnymede in June 1215 under duress from his rebellious barons, restating customary limits on royal authority — protections of the church, restraints on arbitrary taxation, due-process safeguards for free men. Annulled almost immediately by Pope Innocent III, it was reissued repeatedly through the thirteenth century and entered English statute under Edward I in 1297, becoming a touchstone for later constitutional argument.
